  "text": "The constable read the first letter twice. Then he looked up at the woman on the steps.

“You were seven,” he said.

“I was seven when I wrote it.”

He opened the next. The child came through the doorway, leaving small puddles on the boards. She stopped beside Ada and watched the woman with the same grave expression the woman wore.

The constable read on. Once, he pressed a thumb against the paper as if to keep a line from disappearing. The coat hung motionless by the stair. Even the letters still in Venn’s hand had gone quiet.

At the fifth envelope, the constable sat down. “I thought you’d stopped writing.”

“The gate was locked,” the woman said again, more gently than the coat had.

He turned the final envelope over. There was no address, only a date from the previous winter. Inside was a single sheet. He read it, folded it carefully, and held it out toward her.

“I can’t give back the years,” he said.

She came down one step. The child moved forward too, then hesitated where the wet boards met the dry.

“No,” the woman said. “But you can open the gate.”

The key lifted from his shoulder. It crossed the hall slowly, casting a turning shadow on the wall, and settled in his hand.

Outside, beyond the rain, Ada heard metal strike metal. The sound came from far down the street, though she could see no gate from the door.

The constable stood. He took the child’s cold hand, and together they went to find it."
